r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: THE ENSURE_ASCII QUESTION, measured. Three shipped SPINE templates carry non-ASCII: COMMANDER_SPINE (34 chars), EXPLORER_SPINE (13), ADMIRAL_SPINE (12) -- em dashes and middle dots. json.dumps defaults ensure_ascii=True, so the written spine now escapes every one of them: the instantiated Commander spine holds 0 non-ASCII characters and 34 backslash-u escapes where the old verbatim write held 34 literal characters. What does NOT change: parsed content is identical, key order is preserved with origin appended last, exactly one trailing newline as before, and rendered text round-trips to the same characters -- so what the engine prints and what an agent reads is unchanged. What does change: the file bytes. The written spine is also REFORMATTED, which is the larger effect (30801 -> 34660 bytes for the Commander spine; the escapes account for only ~170 of that). Templates hand-format condition dicts on one line; json.dumps(indent=2) expands each onto multiple lines. I found no consumer that reads a written spine as raw text -- no script and no shipped check command greps spine.json -- and the suite is green, so nothing observable breaks today. It is a real behaviour change to record: any future raw-text grep or byte-diff over an instantiated spine sees escaped, reflowed JSON. MAP IMPACT verified against the diff: map/INDEX.md drops scripts.verify_worktree_precondition_coverage, adds tests.test_spine_origin_isolation, and adjusts entity counts; nothing unrelated. The implementer's Map Impact notes match what the diff does. COLLISION AUDIT (audited, not fixed): the failure reproduces and is the only one. Reason #1 of the no-bypass ruling is FALSE as stated -- run_crew.launch_process at scripts/run_crew.py:676 calls subprocess.run(argv, input=, stdout=, stderr=, env=) with no cwd=, and cwd appears nowhere else in that module, so a crew inherits the dispatcher's cwd. Verb scope cannot resolve it: door B drives claim, start, attach, advance; start/attach/advance are all in MUTATING_VERBS, so dropping claim only moves the failure one call down. Option 3 (door supplies SPINE.parent's toplevel as the measured side) is not a real fix: I measured it -- for a spine that init_work_area created at <root>/.agent-work/<id>/spine.json, git rev-parse --show-toplevel from SPINE.parent returns exactly the stamped origin.worktree, equal by construction, because both derive from the same creation act. It is not literally the falsified X == X, since one side is stored text and the other a filesystem fact, but it can only ever fire if the spine FILE is later moved between trees, and it stops measuring where the ACTOR is -- which is the protected intent. I found no honest fix inside the implementer's allowed scope: every real fix changes who sets cwd (run_crew passing cwd=, or the door chdir-ing around the in-process call), and both files are excluded.
